# Swift shell with embedded Python helper over XPC in a sandboxed app — facts

## Definitions

- [statement] Python-Apple-support's macOS framework is a relocatable re-bundling of the official macOS build with IDLE, Tkinter and turtle removed and the App Store compliance patch applied; its main branch builds Python 3.15, with 3.11-3.13 on branches, for macOS 11+ on x86_64 and arm64. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02) — https://github.com/beeware/Python-Apple-support · keywords: Swift shell with embedded Python helper over XPC in a sandboxed app

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] com.apple.security.inherit does not apply to XPC services: they keep a separate sandbox and container, so a service cannot read files in the host app bundle unless the app passes access (a plain bookmark worked where security-scoped bookmarks failed in the 2016 write-up). (medium confidence) (verified as of 2016-08-17) — https://www.mattrajca.com/2016/08/17/accessing-resources-from-an-xpc-services-host-app-in-the-sandbox.html · keywords: Swift shell with embedded Python helper over XPC in a sandboxed app · also: https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/MacOSX/Conceptual/BPSystemStartup/Chapters/CreatingXPCServices.html

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] For XPC helpers under App Sandbox, the app and helper both need app-sandbox enabled, and early guidance paired it with a shared application-groups entitlement; mach-lookup is denied by default in a sandbox, though that write-up concerned a login-item helper rather than an embedded XPC service. (low confidence) (verified as of 2015-01-17) — https://christiantietze.de/posts/2015/01/xpc-helper-sandboxing-mac/ · keywords: Swift shell with embedded Python helper over XPC in a sandboxed app

## Facts and statements

- [statement] XPC services are bundles in Contents/XPCServices of the app bundle, are private to the containing app, and each has its own sandbox and entitlements; by default they run in the most restricted environment, and a service must be code-signed for its entitlements to apply. (medium confidence) — https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/MacOSX/Conceptual/BPSystemStartup/Chapters/CreatingXPCServices.html · keywords: Swift shell with embedded Python helper over XPC in a sandboxed app · also: https://www.mattrajca.com/2016/08/17/accessing-resources-from-an-xpc-services-host-app-in-the-sandbox.html
- [statement] launchd launches XPC services on demand, restarts them after a crash, and kills idle ones with SIGKILL, so a Python helper must be designed stateless or minimal-state; a crash mid-request invalidates the app's connection until launchd restarts the service. Elevating a service to root is unsupported. (low confidence) — https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/MacOSX/Conceptual/BPSystemStartup/Chapters/CreatingXPCServices.html · keywords: Swift shell with embedded Python helper over XPC in a sandboxed app
- [statement] A child tool (NSTask/posix_spawn) that inherits the parent's sandbox must use exactly two sandbox entitlements, com.apple.security.app-sandbox and com.apple.security.inherit; any other sandbox entitlement aborts the child. Xcode 9 injected get-task-allow, which broke inheritance; workarounds were Export Archive or re-signing, and the later Xcode setting CODE_SIGN_INJECT_BASE_ENTITLEMENTS=NO addresses it. (low confidence) (verified as of 2017-09-01) — https://indiestack.com/2017/09/sandbox-inheritance-tax/ · keywords: Swift shell with embedded Python helper over XPC in a sandboxed app
- [statement] Embedding the Python interpreter as a signed framework (BeeWare Python-Apple-support Python.xcframework plus python-stdlib, loaded via PythonKit or the C API) avoids removing the sandbox or disabling library validation; every .so in the stdlib must be re-signed with the team ID and hardened runtime, and PYTHONHOME/PYTHONPATH must be set before Py_Initialize(). (medium confidence) (verified as of 2022-12-03) — https://dev.to/eldare/embedding-python-interpreter-inside-a-macos-app-and-publish-to-the-app-store-successfully-4bop · keywords: Swift shell with embedded Python helper over XPC in a sandboxed app · also: https://github.com/beeware/Python-Apple-support
- [statement] Python 3.12+ ships the string 'itms-services' in Lib/urllib/parse.py, which Apple's automated scan flagged under Guideline 2.5.2 and rejected macOS and iOS apps bundling Python; CPython added a --with-app-store-compliance configure option (PR #120984, refined in #121947) and backported it to 3.12 and 3.13. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02) — https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/120522 · keywords: Swift shell with embedded Python helper over XPC in a sandboxed app · also: https://github.com/beeware/Python-Apple-support
